title: Strata, closed
summary: Your approved strata, with two changes: the opening pass now skims the three layers at about 1.25 seconds each and hands over to the visitor, and the slabs in the drawing are buttons, so pressing a slab opens its row on the right just as pressing a row turns its slab red.
story: Right after the letter's "every quarter starts from zero", this section shows what Kelwin installs instead (three named layers and the one line that keeps what each quarter learned), and it hands the principle a system that now gives off one clear signal.
motion: Standalone: the heading rises in like every other section, with the list on the right and the “Find your weakest layer” link. Then the three layers drop in one at a time, 1.25 seconds apart. Each lands red while it is installed and draws its own mark (lines of text, a route, a ring), and its row on the right opens at the same moment, while the row that was open closes. So: 01 red and Narrative Systems open, then 02 and GTM Infrastructure, then 03 and GTM Intelligence. One beat later the stack closes up and the measurement beside it changes from "3 layers" to "1 system". One line then draws from the bottom layer back up into the top one, ending in an arrow, the ring on the bottom layer closes, and as the arrow lands the red, and its open row, return to 01 and rest there. The whole pass takes about 6.5 seconds (it was 9.5), plays once, and nothing loops afterwards. The slab drops, the close-up and the return line keep their original speed; only the wait between layers is shorter.

On the homepage: the list and the link arrive with the heading, so there is always something to read. The drawing's pass plays once, when about a third of it is in view. Nothing pins: the page scrolls normally, and scrolling away and back does not replay it.

Interaction, both ways: every slab in the drawing is a button, and so is every row in the list. Pressing a slab (click, tap, Enter or Space) moves the red to it and lifts it, brightens its label beside the drawing and opens its row on the right. Pressing a row does the same to its slab. Pressing a slab's label (for example “02 GTM Infrastructure”) works too. Where one slab overlaps the tip of the next, the slab you see on top is the one you press. During the opening pass a slab responds only once it has started to drop in, so empty space never reacts. The drawing and the list always show the same layer.

Any press on a slab, a label or a row stops the opening pass at once: the drawing finishes where it is and shows the layer you chose, and nothing changes after that unless you press again. Tabbing into the drawing or the list also stops it, so nothing opens or closes while someone is reading with the keyboard.

Hover (mouse): over a slab the pointer becomes a hand, the slab's outline and mark come up to white and its face lifts one shade, its label brightens, and its row's title on the right nudges over slightly, as it does when you hover the row itself. Hovering a row does the same to its slab, so you can see which plate a row belongs to before you press, from either side. The red stays on the selected layer only.

Keyboard: Tab runs through the three slabs from 01 to 03, then the three rows, then the link. A focused slab shows four thin white corner brackets around it. Each slab is announced with its layer name and whether its row is open.

Layout: the list keeps the height of its tallest open row the whole time, so the section, the drawing's frame and the “Find your weakest layer” link never move while rows open and close, in either skin, at any width.
Reduced motion: the finished drawing shows straight away (installed, loop and ring closed, 01 red with its row open), with no timers. Pressing a slab or a row still moves the red and opens that row.
Phones: the drawing sits above the list. Tapping a slab turns it red and opens its row in the list below; the page does not scroll on its own.
addressed: "It switches too slowly from layer to layer … increase the pace of switching before it switches back to the original first layer": the red now moves to the next layer every 1.25 seconds instead of every 2.8, and the whole pass, back to 01, takes about 6.5 seconds instead of 9.5. It reads as a quick tour of the three layers, then leaves the section to the visitor.

"So the user can skim through each layer by themselves": once the pass has rested on 01, nothing moves on its own. The visitor goes through the layers at their own pace from either side, the drawing or the list.

"Make the layer plates inside the artifact clickable themselves … it opens the text block on the right side on its own for that specific layer": done. Click or tap the GTM Infrastructure plate and it turns red and lifts, its label brightens and the GTM Infrastructure row opens in full on the right, with the row that was open closing. The same for the other two plates. Clicking a plate's label beside the drawing does the same.

"And vice versa": pressing a row on the right still turns its plate red. The plate, its label and the open row are always the same layer, whichever side you press and in every frame of the opening pass.
Pressing a plate or a row during the opening pass stops it immediately, so the layer you chose stays open.

The plates show they can be pressed: a hand pointer and a quiet brightening on hover (and the matching row's title nudges over, so you see where it will open), and corner brackets when reached with the keyboard. Only the selected plate is red.
Unchanged: the drawing, the copy, the list and the layout at rest are exactly as you approved them, and the page still never jumps while rows open and close.
notes: ROUND 6 (founder note on 05: faster pass; the plates become controls, both ways). Changes, all inside the approved round-5 design (rest frame pixel-identical at 1440 in both skins): (1) PACE: one beat constant drives the pass: T1 500, STEP 1250. Slab drops 500 / 1750 / 3000ms (was 500 / 3300 / 6100); each slab's inscription, nodes and callout keep their offsets from its drop (02 inks 2000–2550, nodes 2000–2830; 03 ring 3250 for 700ms, node 3900; callouts 900 / 2150 / 3400). Dimension draws at 3400 (label 3700), so "3 layers" reads for ~0.45s before it re-measures. Close-up at T1 + 3·STEP = 4250 (700ms, unchanged), return at +650 = 4900 (1000ms, unchanged; ring closes 800–1300ms in; arrowhead at +850), red and row 01 back at 5750 as the arrow lands, settle 6450. Was 7300 / 7950 / 8800 / 9500. The drop (700ms), close-up (700ms), return draw (1000ms) and accordion (360ms) durations are unchanged: only the dwell between layers shrank. demoMs 7000 (final shot after settle). (2) SLAB CONTROLS: pointer and touch go to the visible slab faces themselves (top and sides, pointer-events: visible, cursor pointer), so the slab painted on top is the one pressed: 01's front tip covers 02's back tip (and 02's covers 03's), most of all when the selected slab lifts 8px; a transparent hit layer painted over the drawing would hand those overlaps to the slab underneath (review measured up to ~700px² of wrong target), so it takes no pointer. A slab that has not dropped in yet takes nothing (is-wait on the slab during the pass; live(n) clears it as each drops). Keyboard and assistive tech: a hit layer over the drawing (svg g.km-system-T__hits, pointer-events none), one g[role=button][tabindex=0] per slab in reading order 01 → 03 (the visible slabs stay painted 03 → 01 for occlusion, so they could not carry focus order themselves). Each holds a transparent silhouette path (for the screen reader's focus rect) and a corner-bracket focus path, inside a lift group; it rides the exploded/installed transform through the existing [data-l] rule and the 8px lift through is-on, so the focus brackets always sit on their slab. aria-label 'Layer 0n, <name>', aria-controls = the row's panel id, aria-expanded mirrors the row, aria-disabled on the open one (same accordion pattern as the row heads). Enter on keydown, Space on keyup (keydown prevented, no page scroll); click also activates (a screen reader's press). The svg is now role=group (keeps the long drawing description, plus 'Each slab is a button that opens its layer in the list'); the decorative groups are aria-hidden. The anno layer is pointer-events:none; the callouts opt back in (pointer only: the slab is the keyboard stop). show(n) also sets the hits' is-on/aria-expanded/aria-disabled, so slab, hit, callout, current-row rule and open row move together. activate(n) = finish() if the pass is running, then show(n): used by slab, callout, hit and row presses. focusin on the drawing or the ledger also finishes the pass. (3) HOVER: mouse/pen only (pointerenter, pointerType != touch, so taps leave nothing behind): slab, callout or row n sets is-hover on slab n (top outline and inscription to --fg, sides to --fg-2, top face fill --panel, 200ms), on callout n (label to --fg) and on row n (the kit's own 6px title nudge, so a slab hover previews its row). Never on the selected slab's face, never red. FOCUS: four 12px corner brackets, 1px --fg, 8px outside the slab's bounding box, on :focus-visible only (a mouse click focuses the slab without them). TESTS (work/system-r6; review pass in rv-*.mjs: un-landed slabs take no pointer; 0 visual/pointer mismatches over 16,000 sampled points per selection; human-speed presses at 1.3–5.3s stop the pass; touch at 390 and 760; page context at 1280 zoomed and 1440): seq.mjs records every frame of the pass: 0 out-of-sync frames (selected layer, red slab, slab button state and aria-expanded, bright callout, current row, open row, row aria-expanded) at 1440 and 390; section 1343.8px and 1860.9px constant; door constant after its entrance rise. interact.mjs: a click on slab 02 at 1.3s (01 still red) jumps to rest with 02 red and open, nothing changes after 7s more; slab / callout / row presses in turn stay in sync with the door and section fixed; hover and leave; mouse click shows no brackets; Tab order slabs 01–03 → rows 01–03 → link; Tab into the drawing at 2.0s stops the pass on 02; Enter and Space work on slabs with no scroll; reduced motion: zero class changes over 4s and slab presses work. touch.mjs (390, touch): taps on slabs mid-pass and at rest, no hover left, no horizontal scroll. homeseq.mjs (stitched letter/system/principle at 1280×720, zoomed): waits for 30% in view, plays in sync, does not replay; slab clicks hit the right slab under the page zoom. focusrest.mjs: brackets and hover in both skins. mk PASS (strict); no console errors. COPY unchanged. RED MAP unchanged: label square, rule, note label square, and the selected slab's top face. PRODUCTION: show(n) stays one state value; the hit layer maps to one <button>-like element per slab (or a <g role=button>), with the same timings expressed as STEP-based constants in Motion. History: round 5 made the list follow the red (one show(n) for slab, callout and row), reserved the ledger's tallest height so nothing jumps, and removed the title-block labels under the drawing. Promoted from round-2 slot U.
